Adopt

Add one capability across operating systems, libraries, and services

Applications already use abstractions for files, windows, networks, and libraries. OA extends that idea to running capabilities such as downloads, model calls, logging, storage, configuration, and application tools. Choose the capability, add its client, run the OA service, and connect an available implementation.

OpenAbstractions 0.8.0 release notes list available packages, included features and installation verification. For source integrations, Language support shows which modules each language can call and the platform each call was checked on.

For people who use applications

Install the shared runtime

Install OpenAbstractions 0.8.0. The release notes list each asset's contents and package verification, including Panel availability.

Install app integrations from the Panel's Catalog; double-clicking their MSIs is not supported yet. Agent MCP connections after an upgrade from 0.4 are deferred to 0.8.1. Smart App Control can block the bundled llama.cpp engine and the official OpenCode installer. Read the known issues before upgrading.

Windows

For OpenAbstractions 0.8.0, download OpenAbstractions-Setup-0.8.0.exe from the release assets, compare it with SHA256SUMS and run it. Setup installs the runtime and the Panel. The Panel's Apps Catalog installs OpenCode through its official installer and adds the OpenAbstractions integration to an existing ComfyUI. The x64 and ARM64 MSIs install the core runtime directly. They default to Just me. Everyone requires administrator access. Adding commands to PATH is optional.

Linux

Download the amd64 or ARM64 archive from the latest runtime release, extract it and follow its install.sh instructions for the current user. See the release notes for installation verification and platform limits.

macOS

Download the universal package from the latest runtime release when the release attaches one. Its notes identify the signing state, tested systems and installation checks.

The release notes state each asset's signing outcome and the architectures its installation was tested on. Check the downloads against the release SHA256SUMS before installing:

sha256sum -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS

In PowerShell, hash Setup and find its line in SHA256SUMS:

(Get-FileHash OpenAbstractions-Setup-0.8.0.exe -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLower()
Select-String OpenAbstractions-Setup-0.8.0.exe SHA256SUMS

After installation, check the runtime from a terminal. If you left PATH unchanged, use the installed executable’s full path.

openabstractions status --json
openabstractions probe --json

status reports readiness; probe checks bounded service reads. status --json prints each capability's readiness as one JSON document. probe --json prints one JSON document per probe result. An application still needs permission for its requested actions and a compatible provider. The installation guide describes setup.

Installed runtime features

The Windows installer offers feature choices. Check the release notes to see which optional tools are included in each asset before configuring an assistant.

FeatureInstallsDefaultWhat it does
RuntimeThe service, Panel and command lineOn—
Local model storesinventoryd.exe and the declaration file that registers it as an abstraction.storage/inventory-source@1 providerOnFinds the model files your other apps already downloaded.
MCP gatewayopenabstractions-mcp, with no runtime declaration (unlike the other features, it installs no declaration file in tools\declarations\, so the runtime does not know it exists or start it; an assistant launches it directly by its path, and it holds no rights until granted)OffLets an AI assistant use OA's tools.
Model hostmodelhostd.exe only; openabstractions models host writes its provider declaration laterOffServes chat and embeddings from a model file on this machine with the pinned llama.cpp build, which modelhostd engine install stages from the publisher's archive you download.

Local model stores are on by default because they only read directory listings and write nothing. The MCP gateway and model host default to off. Selecting either installs its program but grants it no rights; the gateway has no runtime declaration, and a model-host declaration is written when an operator configures a model.

What changes after installing

The runtime starts as a background service. On Windows, a Panel icon sits in the notification area at sign-in, and the Panel also opens from the Start menu. The first time an application asks for a new permission, the Panel shows the question. On Windows, the Panel's Apps Catalog installs or repairs OpenCode and installs the OpenAbstractions integration for ComfyUI. The Device page shows storage by type, free space, the largest reported items and verified duplicates. See the application guide.

Manage credentials from the Panel

The Panel's Credentials page stores secrets your applications use, without ever showing, logging or sending a value back to you. Its own "Learn more" and "?" links open the anchors below; the same steps are available from the command line.

Saved credentials

Lists every credential registered on this account by name, kind, state, target and consumer; the secret itself is never shown, logged or sent back.

openabstractions credentials list

Add credential

Registers a new secret under a name that is not already in use, scoped to the hosts it may be sent to and the services allowed to apply it. The credential manager binds the caller the same way for every write (CRED-H1).

openabstractions credentials add <name> --target HOST --for CONSUMER

Rotate

Replaces the secret and expiry of a credential you have already listed, at the revision the list showed.

openabstractions credentials rotate <name>

Revoke

Deletes a credential's secret immediately and keeps a tombstone recording that it existed, at the revision you already listed.

openabstractions credentials revoke <name>

App access

Sets whether one application on one account may apply a named credential, using the same rights rule editor as the Panel's Questions and permissions page. Check and Apply evaluate the rights rule before the request is ever sent (CRED-A2).

openabstractions credentials allow <name> --program PATH, or add --deny

For developers

Quickstart: send a log record to OA

This quickstart runs on Windows with Go 1.26 or newer. Your program sends one structured record to the shared log service, and the Panel shows it.

  1. Install the runtime with OpenAbstractions Setup.
  2. Create a module and add the logging client: 
    mkdir my-app
cd my-app
go mod init example.com/my-app
go get github.com/openabstractions/abstraction-logging/go@v0.8.0
  3. Save this as main.go: 
    package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "log"
    "log/slog"
    "time"

    logging "github.com/openabstractions/abstraction-logging/go"
)

func main() {
    h := logging.Default("my-app")
    slog.SetDefault(slog.New(h))
    slog.Info("worker started", "component", "indexer")

    // Close drains the queued records before the program exits. With no OA
    // runtime it returns the resolution error, and log.Fatal prints it.
    ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
    defer cancel()
    counts, err := h.Close(ctx)
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    fmt.Printf("sent %d record to OA\n", counts.Written)
}
  4. Build and run it: 
    go build -o app.exe .
.\app.exe
  5. It prints: 
    sent 1 record to OA
  6. Open the Panel, go to Activity and expand Detailed log. The record reads my-app: worker started. Once your app is a registered application, openabstractions logs --app NAME prints its records in a terminal, and --follow keeps printing new ones.

Choose a capability

Work and data

Jobs retain accepted work. Downloads dedupe by digest in one job table and delegate the transfer. Storage finds content-addressed bytes.

Example: a program recovers the same download after it restarts.

Application services

Logging carries structured events. Configuration exposes effective OA settings and the source of each value. Credentials keep secrets inside approved services.

Example: the OA Panel follows logs and configuration changes while an application runs.

Models and inference

Model describes model lookup. Router selects eligible hosts. Inference carries chat, embeddings, speech, transcription, live sessions, and image generation.

A chat completion needs inference alone.

Example: a coding assistant keeps its chat API while OA changes the selected provider.

People, programs, and apps

Identity identifies the connected program and account. Rights chooses what that program may do. Asks carries specific human decisions. The facade can list visible apps and open a registered app with permission.

Example: the first time a program uses a saved credential, OA asks the person in the Panel, and the program's retry succeeds once they allow it.

For provider authors

Compare-and-set (CAS) replaces shared bytes only when they still match the version a provider read. Watch turns polled or pushed values into current snapshots, reports quiet after a chosen budget, and can collapse a burst into one settled callback.

Providers use these development utilities directly through their language packages. CAS has no behavioral contract page or capability claim.

Open the capability catalogue

Resolve a service

ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
defer cancel()

sink, err := facade.Discover().ResolveLog(
    ctx,
    facade.Requirements{Scope: facade.ScopeLocal},
)
  1. Choose an explicit deadline and execution scope.
  2. Request only the guarantees your feature requires.
  3. Handle resolution errors and capability outcomes as normal product states.
  4. Save the returned work reference and use the same request identity when a submission reply is lost.
  5. Exercise forbidden, unavailable, interruption, restart, and stale-context behavior for your integration.

Choose a language client

All five languages can use the shared native connection. Go, Python and C++ include it in the default facade entry point. Rust and JavaScript use separate native connector packages; their installed-runtime paths select and verify runtime identity. The facade repository gives revision-specific setup. The Language support page records checks per module and language. Runtime packaging and release qualification remain separate from these source paths.

Python wheels, Rust crates and npm packages have their own source versions and publication status, separate from the runtime release. The capability source remains available in its repository.

Ship OA with your app

Your Windows installer checks for the runtime and runs OpenAbstractions Setup when it is missing or older than the version your app needs.

Detect the runtime. The installer records version and ipc_library under Software\OpenAbstractions\Abstraction, in HKLM for a machine install and in HKCU for a Just me install:

Get-ItemProperty "HKLM:\Software\OpenAbstractions\Abstraction" | Select-Object version, ipc_library
version ipc_library
------- -----------
0.8.0   C:\Program Files\OpenAbstractions\tools\abstraction_ipc.dll

Check the version. Compare version with the lowest release your client modules need. For modules at v0.8.0, that is 0.8.0. openabstractions status --json reports whether each capability resolves, and exits with 0 when all of them do.

Run Setup. Bundle OpenAbstractions-Setup-0.8.0.exe or download it from the release, check its SHA-256, and run it from your installer. Setup accepts the standard WiX Burn switches: /passive shows progress only, /quiet shows no window, /norestart defers a restart, and /log <file> writes a log. Setup installs the runtime for the whole machine and asks for administrator approval once.

OpenAbstractions-Setup-0.8.0.exe /passive /norestart /log oa-setup.log

When the person declines. Setup exits with a nonzero code and installs nothing. Let your app install and start anyway. Each Resolve* call then returns a resolution error, and your app shows its OA features as unavailable until the person runs Setup.

ComfyUI: install the node

On Windows, the Panel's Apps Catalog installs the OpenAbstractions integration into a ComfyUI installation from ComfyUI's official source.

The node is an ordinary ComfyUI custom node, described by its own pyproject.toml. Its [tool.comfy] table holds the Comfy Registry fields: PublisherId, DisplayName and requires-comfyui, the lowest ComfyUI version the node has run against. A Comfy Registry listing waits for a publisher account.

[tool.comfy]
PublisherId = "openabstractions"
DisplayName = "OpenAbstractions Downloads"
requires-comfyui = ">=0.35.0"

If OA is not running, Manager keeps working as before and the node explains what is missing rather than failing silently.

OpenCode: one command

On Windows, the Panel's Apps Catalog installs or repairs OpenCode.

The integration ships configure.js, and the Catalog runs it for you. It reads the router's servable chat families through the runtime and writes or updates the provider.<id> block. If no default model is set, it also selects one of those families. Other configuration keys stay untouched, and running it again with nothing changed leaves the file unchanged. The installed copy is in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\OpenAbstractions\apps\opencode\plugin\0.8.0\. The OpenCode adapter guide lists its flags.

Connect an assistant through the MCP gateway

How application MCP works: the developing application profile, shared state and action semantics, and current availability.

The MCP gateway is a separate optional stdio program. When the selected asset includes it, an assistant launches it directly. The gateway source and guide describe its tools and permission model.

The gateway guide includes source-build commands, permission setup and an OpenCode configuration example. Check the release notes to confirm whether the selected asset contains the optional program.

Application editing requires an application-specific adapter. For example, the ComfyUI experiment supplies preview, apply and readback tools tied to a document revision. The gateway’s application-listing tool exposes discovery metadata. See how application interaction fits together.
